cells.title: Name the waggledance CLI first in the cross-project refusal
cells.action: Implement docs/history/waggledance-cli-first/CONTEXT.md D4 with D2 and D8, keeping D3 and D5. In fn refusal in cross_project.rs (anchor: `FIX: call waggledance_ask_state for that project, then waggledance_dispatch with leader: true so its own leader does the work.`) replace that one FIX sentence with exactly: `FIX: hand it to that project's own leader: run waggledance state <project-id>, then waggledance dispatch --project <project-id> --leader --request-id <id> --task "<task>" (the project id from waggledance list --json, never a path); if the waggledance CLI is missing, does not know the verb, is refused, or fails, call waggledance_ask_state for that project, then waggledance_dispatch with leader: true and the same request_id.` Every other sentence of the refusal, the supervisor sentences, the registry read (`waggledance list --json`) and every function signature stay unchanged. Red first in write_guard/tests.rs: in fn cp_refused add asserts that stderr contains `waggledance state`, `waggledance dispatch --project`, `--leader`, `--request-id` and `request_id` (keep the existing asserts for waggledance_ask_state, waggledance_dispatch, leader: true and guards.cross_project_allow), and update fn refusal_text_for_test to the new sentence; run the cross_project tests and watch the new asserts fail before you change cross_project.rs. The string `wg ` must not appear in the refusal. No code comments. One commit with the trailer `cell: wcli-1`.

cells.title: Name the waggledance CLI first in doctrine, skills and handbook
cells.action: Implement docs/history/waggledance-cli-first/CONTEXT.md D1, D2, D3, D7 and D8 in the hand-authored homes, ASD-STE100 style, short sentences. (1) packages/bee/LEADER.md, rule block agents-other-project-to-its-leader: keep the marker lines and the never-read and cross_project_allow sentences; say the agent uses the waggledance CLI first: `waggledance state <project-id>`, then `waggledance dispatch --project <project-id> --leader --request-id <id>` with the task through `--task`, `--task-file` or stdin (add `--follow-up-of <run>` when a `leaders[].runs` row of the state output shows its leader already runs the same work; add `--handoff` for a handoff); `<project-id>` is the `id` field of `waggledance list --json`; output is JSON. The MCP tools are the fallback: `waggledance_ask_state`, then `waggledance_dispatch` with `leader: true` (`follow_up_of`, `handoff: true`) and the SAME `request_id`, called when the `waggledance` binary is not on PATH, does not know the verb (`unrecognized subcommand`, exit 2), a guard or permission refuses the shell call, or it fails with a tool error; the shared request id means a fallback never starts a second run; with `--task-file` the fallback passes the file text as `task`. `<project-id>` is never a path, and a task file stays inside this project. Never call `wg`. This rule block is the one home of the mapping and the fallback (D7). (2) packages/bee/playbooks/handoff.md, skills/bee-hive/references/go-mode.md, skills/bee-swarming/SKILL.md, skills/bee-swarming/references/swarming-reference.md and docs/handbook/stages/swarming.md: where each says `waggledance: waggledance_dispatch with leader: true and follow_up_of ... plus handoff: true`, name the CLI call first — `waggledance dispatch --project <this project id> --leader --follow-up-of <current run> --handoff --request-id <id>` with the task through `--task`, `--task-file` or stdin — and say the MCP fallback follows rule agents-other-project-to-its-leader; use the same CLI string byte for byte in all five homes; keep every other sentence. (3) docs/config-reference.md, section guards.cross_project_allow: the remedy names `waggledance state` then `waggledance dispatch --leader` first, with `waggledance_ask_state` / `waggledance_dispatch` as the fallback. (4) Run `.bee/bin/bee dev regen` and keep every file it rewrites; list each in the cap. If regen rewrites a file outside this cell's list, name it as a scope deviation. Do not edit docs/knowledge (wcli-3 owns it) or any Rust file (wcli-1 owns them). No `wg` anywhere. One commit with the trailer `cell: wcli-2`.

truths: Rule agents-other-project-to-its-leader names waggledance state and waggledance dispatch --leader first and the MCP tools as the fallback
The rule names the four fallback triggers: binary missing, unknown verb, refused shell call, tool error, and one request id shared by the CLI call and its MCP fallback
Every handoff home names waggledance dispatch --leader --follow-up-of --handoff first and cites the rule for the fallback
The rendered copies match the sources after bee dev regen
